settings.headline: Spray suits a specific kind of procedure.
settings.body: Spray covers ground that cream can't. Body areas, larger treatment zones, injection sites where a sprayed application is faster and more practical. Spray sits at Advanced and Professional strengths only — the procedures that suit a spray format don't tend to call for an entry-tier preparation.

settings.body: Most aesthetic appointments end with a treated area that needs gentle handling. The Senseless Foaming Cleanser is built for the hours after. An antibacterial cleansing foam that respects what you just had done.
settings.image_alt: Editorial image of the Senseless Foaming Cleanser on a clean countertop

settings.question: Why no Clinical spray?
settings.answer: The procedures that suit spray format tend to be the ones already past entry-tier preparation — body areas, injection sites, larger treatment zones. Spray starts at Advanced because that's where the format genuinely begins to be useful. We could make a Clinical spray. We don't, because we don't see the indication for it.

settings.question: Cream, gel, or spray — how do I choose?
settings.answer: Spray covers ground the other two don't. Cream and gel are face-and-small-area formats. Spray suits body work, broader zones, or injection-led procedures. See choose your format.

settings.question: When do I apply spray?
settings.answer: Ahead of your appointment. Your practitioner is the best guide for the specific procedure you've booked.

settings.question: Is spray stronger than cream or gel?
settings.answer: Strength is independent of format. An Advanced spray is the same concentration as an Advanced cream. Spray is a different application, not a different strength system.

settings.question: Is this a medicine?
settings.answer: No. Senseless is a UK cosmetic product. Not a medicine. Not a pharmacy product.
